per_prediction.description: Research relies on only two benchmark datasets (QM9 and ZINC), ignoring a wide range of established drug‑discovery datasets.
The literature lacks any reported work on molecular property prediction (e.g., solubility, toxicity, bioactivity) using GNNs.
No studies have applied variational autoencoders (VAE) or generative adversarial networks (GAN) on graph structures for de novo molecular generation and optimization.
Self‑supervised pretraining on large molecular graphs is absent from the surveyed literature.
Explainability and interpretability of GNN predictions in drug design are completely absent from the surveyed claims.
Graph representation learning for protein–ligand interaction prediction has received no attention in the current corpus.
Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNN) are mentioned only conceptually, with no empirical comparisons to newer architectures such as GCN or GAT in drug‑discovery tasks.
